AI models can explain U.S. immigration law, but what happens when the law changes?

On Immigration Bench, frontier models met just 7.3% of expert criteria on 2025–2026 immigration rules compared to 64.0% on established law. Recent policy changes are a major blind spot, even for the strongest models.

Models by @GoogleDeepMind scale better on cost than their rivals.

Gemini 4 Carbon is the prime example. As tasks get more demanding, every rival gets more expensive relative to Carbon.

For a typical task, GPT-6 Astra by @OpenAI costs 3.4× as much, Claude Opus 5.5 by @AnthropicAI costs 3.9× as much, and GPT-6.1 Sol is the cheaper option at about half of Carbon’s cost (0.54×).

Across the 5% most expensive sessions, Carbon’s position improves against all three. Opus edges up to 4.2×, Astra’s cost roughly doubles relative to Carbon, and Sol’s discount shrinks.

This in turn can translate into meaningful savings across real-world tasks such as building an Android security app, one of many long-horizon tasks that our Agent Arena users delegate to their agents.

GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst and Flare by @OpenAI are here, running almost 2x faster than GPT Image 2.5.

In the Text-to-Image Arena, Sunburst (Medium) is #2 with 1409 pts, and Flare (Medium) #4 with 1384 pts! By category, Sunburst landed #1 in Cartoon, Anime & Fantasy.

In the Image Edit Arena, Sunburst (Medium) is #3 with 1476 pts, and Flare (Medium) #5 with 1462 pts. See leaderboard in thread.

With this release, @OpenAI remains the #1 lab in both arenas and holds all top 5 Text-to-Image spots!

GPT Image 2.6 lands on Arena with enhanced speed. According to @OpenAI, Sunburst (Medium) and Flare (Medium) are more than 2x faster than GPT Image 2.5 while maintaining the lead over competing labs. They report similar quality to Image 2.5, with enhanced photorealism, greater editing consistency, and a dynamic reasoning level that enables latency as low as 5 seconds. Find more details at their blog linked below.

Congrats to the @OpenAI team on this release!

Exciting news: @Kimi_Moonshot has released the open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro, now #1 among open models in Agent Arena!

Across 17.5K+ real-world, long-horizon agentic sessions from our global community of users, Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max) delivers +5.1% net improvement, ranking #1 open and #13 overall.

It ranks #1 among open models in all three categories: Work, Code, and Chat.

This is a +4.2 percentage point improvement over Kimi K3 (Max), with +0.9% (#6 open). It also improved across all signals. Among open models, it ranks:
- #1 in Bash Reliability (successful shell commands) with +7.9%: (up from K3 at #13 with −4.5%).
- #1 in Praise vs Complaint (sentiment in user reactions) with +7.7%: (up from K3 at #6 with +1.3%).
- #1 in Steerability (responding to user corrections) with +6.5%: (up from K3 at #5 with +0.4%).
- #4 in Confirmed Success (explicit “yes, that worked” from users) with +3.9%: (from K3 at #5 with +3.8%).

Congrats to @Kimi_Moonshot on this contribution to the open ecosystem!

Big news: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash by @GoogleAI debuts at #1 in both Text-to-Video and Image-to-Video, and #3 in Video Edit!

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash landed #1 in Text-to-Video with 1541 pts. This is a +27 pt improvement from the previous Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash at #2 with 1514 pts.

With this release, Google’s Omni variants take all 3 top slots in Text-to-Video.

See the Image-to-Video and Video Edit results in thread.

Congrats to the @GoogleAI team on this release!

As tasks get more complex, @GoogleDeepMind and @XiaomiMiMo are the biggest winners in the Agent Arena.

On cheaper tasks, @OpenAI and @AnthropicAI hold 10 of the 11 frontier spots. On the most expensive 5% of sessions, they hold just 7. The freed spots go to Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.6 Flash and Pro.

These shifts matter as sessions costing $100 or more are not uncommon across real-world use cases coming from Agent Arena. Even within the last 2 weeks, more than 1,000 sessions crossed that boundary, and choosing a suboptimal model might have had a meaningful impact on that final bill.

Hy4 from Tencent scores 35 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 and is the #2 model from a China-based AI lab

Hy4 is the latest model from @TencentHunyuan and is the successor to Hy3 released earlier this year. It scores 35 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, equal with Grok 4.7 (xhigh) and 1 point behind Claude Haiku 5.5 (max). Hy4 is the #2 model from a China-based AI lab, behind only Kimi K3.1 Pro, which scores 46. Hy4 is priced at $0.834/$2.501 per 1M input/output tokens.

Key takeaways:

➤ Hy4 excels at agentic coding tasks. Hy4 scores 31% on FrontierCode 2.0, compared to 32% for Claude Fable 5.1 (max). It is the leading model from a China-based AI lab, with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) scoring 28% and Kimi K3.1 Pro scoring 25%. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, it scores 37%, the fourth-highest score among models from China-based AI labs

➤ Hy4 outperforms its peers on knowledge and reasoning. Hy4 achieves accuracy of 50% on AA-Omniscience v1.1, 1 point ahead of Kimi K3.1 Pro, but has a high hallucination rate of 89% compared to Kimi K3.1 Pro’s 37%. On HLE-Diamond, it scores 33% compared to Kimi K3.1 Pro’s 37%

➤ Hy4 offers a competitive Capability vs. Cost trade-off compared to to peers. With a Cost per Intelligence Index Task of $0.78, Hy4 (35) is 10-times cheaper than Grok 4.7 (xhigh, 35) and 13-times cheaper than Qwen3.8 Max (0902) (34) but almost twice as expensive as Claude Haiku 5.5 (max, 36)

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens

➤ Pricing: $0.834/$2.501 per 1M input/output tokens. Cache reads $0.042 per 1M tokens

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, with text output

A $100 budget buys 40 Intelligence Index tasks (a mix of task archetypes) with Opus 5.5 at medium reasoning effort, or 10 tasks at max effort. The same $100 is 166 tasks with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) or 2,500 with GPT-6 Luna (medium). https://t.co/fxgRJZzuTv

Nanbeige has released Nanbeige4.3-33B, an open weights model matching Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 with stronger terminal use but weaker knowledge

@Nanbeige is the foundation model research team at BOSS Zhipin, the Chinese recruitment platform operated by Kanzhun Limited. Its dense 33B reasoning model is open weights under Apache 2.0, with text input and output only, a 524K-token context window, and is small enough to run locally on a laptop.

Key results:

➤ Competitive results at ~30B total parameters. Nanbeige4.3-33B and Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) both score 20, compared with 6 for Muse Glimmer (high, 30B).

➤ Terminal use and physics reasoning are relative strengths. Nanbeige scores 30% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 16% on CritPt v2's Hard Subset, vs. 6% and 4% respectively for Qwen3.8 27B.

➤ Different strengths to Qwen3.8 27B despite the same overall score. Nanbeige beats Qwen3.8 27B on AutomationBench-AA (53% vs. 48%), but trails on AA-Briefcase v1.1 (1162 vs. 1391 Elo), FrontierCode 2.0 (11% vs. 15%) and HLE-Diamond (7% vs. 15%).

➤ High abstention and low hallucination rates on Omniscience. Nanbeige scores -4 on AA-Omniscience v1.1 vs. -6 for Qwen3.8 27B, with a hallucination rate of 18% vs. 29%. It answers fewer questions correctly (12% vs. 17%) and declines 71% of questions.

➤ Similar intelligence with more output tokens per task. Nanbeige used 158K output tokens per Intelligence Index task vs. 110K for Qwen3.8 27B, about 44% more.

Additional model details:

➤ Type: Open weights reasoning (Apache 2.0 license)

➤ Size: 33B total parameters (dense)

➤ Modalities: Text input and output only

➤ Context window: 524K

➤ API availability: No confirmed public first- or third-party APIs

In AA-PersonalityBench, MiMo-V2.6-Pro ends 34% of its responses with a question, the highest share of any model measured

The share of responses that end with a question ranges from 34% down to 0% across the models measured. Six models end fewer than 0.5% of their responses with a question.

Share of responses that end with a question:

➤ Most often: MiMo-V2.6-Pro (34%), GPT-6 Astra (32%), GPT-6.1 Sol (29%), Muse Glimmer (28%) and Muse Spark Open (26%)

➤ Least often: GPT-5.4 mini (0.0%), Nemotron 3 Ultra (0.0%), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (0.1%), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (0.1%), GPT-3.5 Turbo (0.2%) and Grok 4.7 (0.4%)

People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.

Some news: I’m joining OpenAI to lead product management for Core Products!

I have a lot of respect for OpenAI for showing the world that scaling works, for bringing AI to over a billion people, and for believing great products are core to the mission.

I’m excited to work with @thsottiaux, an incredible PM team, and everyone across OpenAI. Together, we’ll build agents that have your back and your team’s, and keep you in control, so you get more time for the people and work you love.

Lots to learn, and lots to build. Please keep your feedback coming!

We will all be learning in coming weeks & months, that most human-made software:

▫️ Was really slow
▫️ Had many security vulnerabilities
▫️ Was under-specified and incorrect

AI will rewrite it all. Many times. It will make it fast, cost-efficient, and secure. It will think about failure modes we couldn't wrap our heads around.

It will prove, formally verify, load test, harden. It will turn memory-unsafe foundations into robust, optimized ones. If you ask, it'll thoroughly document it, teach you about it, make diagrams, animations, and slide decks.

In many ways, we are witnessing the true birth of software engineering.

before writing a lot of code with agents, first ask your agent to create a lint rule that caps how many lines a single code file can have. i typically go with 1000

this is the easiest win that has a lasting impact on the health of your codebase

and do it as early as possible in your project, because unwinding it is costly later on
